I have farmed this land since I was young. My father farmed it before me. I know this soil, I know this weather. I do not need to think much about what to plant — wheat in winter, corn in summer. That is what everyone in Quzhou does. That is what the land here is for.

My wife helps me a little, but at my age I cannot do heavy work myself. My son is in the city. I hire the tractor man from the village for tillage and sometimes for sowing. It costs money but there is no choice.

I have about 3 mu. I used to farm more but I cannot manage it now. I will plant all 3 mu to wheat this autumn and then corn on the same land after harvest — that is the rotation, same as always.

For wheat I go to the village supply store and buy the improved variety they sell. Last year it was Jimai, good yield, no problem. For corn I buy the hybrid seed in the small bags — Zhengdan or something similar, whatever they have. Hybrid corn gives more grain, I have learned that much.

Fertilizer I apply the same as before — compound fertilizer when planting, then urea when the crop is growing. I do not measure carefully, I go by feel and by what I spent last year. I water the wheat four times: once before the ground freezes, once when it starts to joint, once when it heads, and once after. Corn I water maybe twice — after planting if it is dry, and once more in the summer heat. I spray wheat twice, once for weeds in winter, once for the aphids. Corn once is usually enough.

I keep a small patch near the house — half a mu or so — for vegetables. Mainly garlic, cabbage, maybe some peppers. Just for us to eat.
